analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (1–1125) and the bounded patch. Visible changes expand autopilotHistory with a detail field (BASE 343) and add adopted-model, placement-hold and download state after BASE 354. These declarations alone do not establish a security regression. Existing context separates inventory planning from ordinary slot limits (314–319), filters startup advertisements by runtime eligibility (823–840), generates a process X25519 key (842), and retains load-bound artifact/cache identities (939–943). No visible change affects encryption, attestation signing, credential custody, privileged fan authority or billing.
Integration must examine the complete HEAD additions at 356–404 and their consumers in ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement and ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload: whether adopted inventory models still pass verification/eligibility and memory admission before serving (T-012/T-027, TB-007), whether holds expire without stranding resources (T-029), and whether download-trigger authority and storage/resource bounds preserve the operator/coordinator boundary. Check new history detail producers and outbound serialization for prompt or identity exposure (A-001/T-058). Cache construction and scope binding remain external to these excerpts; inspect them only where the new serving paths interact with T-041. The patch is truncated and HEAD source and consumers are absent, so authorization, hold lifecycle and download behavior cannot be concluded from stored-state comments. Further integration review is needed, not a finding based on missing controls.
